title: The Battle of Hastings
description: October 1066. William of Normandy's invasion army faces King Harold's Anglo-Saxon shield wall on Senlac Hill. The player commands the Norman force and must break the shield wall through feigned retreats and combined cavalry-archer assaults before nightfall ends the battle.

anachronisms_found: Player Two (Anglo-Saxons) is given a CASTLE, 29 STONE_WALL segments, 4 GUARD_TOWERS and 2 gates on Senlac Hill; Hastings was an open field battle and Harold's army had no fortification whatsoever — castle-building was the Norman innovation, not the Saxon one
A Saxon MONASTERY and dedicated 'Raze the Saxon Castle behind the ridge' objective are pure invention with no counterpart at Hastings
Saxon STABLE and ARCHERY_RANGE imply mounted and missile arms; Harold's force fought dismounted and was notably almost devoid of archers — the archer imbalance was a defining feature of the battle

CHAMPION units (late-medieval two-handed swordsmen in plate) stand in for the huscarls the dialogue names, when the engine's HUSKARL unit is literally the Anglo-Danish housecarl and was the obvious available choice

Norman side is given a TOWN_CENTER, MILL, HOUSES, BLACKSMITH and production buildings — an economic base that did not exist on the field; the Norman camp was a hastily thrown-up beachhead at Pevensey/Hastings, not a settled town

issues_found: Both players' civilizations are set to RANDOM, so architecture and unit rosters may be Aztec, Mongol, Japanese etc. rather than a plausible Frankish/Briton pairing for 11th-century Normandy and England — an entirely avoidable omission.
4,800 TREE_OAK tiles on a 120x120 map turn Senlac Hill into dense forest; the battle was fought on an open ridge above a marshy valley, and the narration itself says 'across the marshy field'.

Player 2 (Anglo-Saxons) is given a CASTLE, 29 STONE_WALL segments, 2 gates and 4 GUARD_TOWERs, plus 'Close Gates' and 'Gate Defense' triggers. Harold's army stood in the open field with no fortification, and stone castles were the Norman innovation the English lacked.
The secondary objective 'Raze the Saxon Castle behind the ridge for additional glory' invents a fortification and an objective that has no basis in the sources.

Harold Godwinson is represented by the generic non-combat KING unit rather than a renamed fighting unit; the historical Harold fought and died in the shield wall, and a KING unit cannot participate in the melee it is meant to anchor.
The Anglo-Saxon player owns a STABLE and an ARCHERY_RANGE, implying mounted and missile arms the English notably did not deploy at Hastings.

The feigned retreat — named in three separate dialogue lines as the decisive tactic — is not implemented in any trigger; the only Saxon movement triggers are a generic PATROL and a sortie on OBJECTS_IN_AREA, so the player never actually executes or benefits from a feint.
The 900-second timer victory would award the Normans the field even if Harold survives, whereas an intact English shield wall at nightfall was precisely the outcome that would have defeated William.

Both players' civilizations are left as RANDOM, so architecture and unit bonuses may render the Normans as Aztecs or Koreans; Franks/Normans and Britons/Celts were available and should have been assigned explicitly.
4,800 oak trees on a 120x120 map turns the open downland of Senlac/Caldbec Hill into dense forest; the battle was fought on bare open slopes with marsh at the foot.

The Anglo-Saxon side is given a CASTLE, 29 STONE_WALL segments, 2 gates and 4 GUARD_TOWERs. Harold's army held an unfortified ridge; there was no fortification at Hastings, and the 'Raze the Saxon Castle' objective invents a structure outright.
Player 2 is given a STABLE and ARCHERY_RANGE, implying Saxon cavalry and archers when the sources are emphatic that Harold's army fought dismounted with almost no archery.
Norman archers (8) are underweighted relative to knights and infantry given that the missile arm was the decisive component of the combined assaults the brief itself stresses.
The defeat condition on the Norman TOWN_CENTER ('beachhead camp has fallen') invents a Saxon counter-raid on Hastings/Pevensey that never occurred during the battle.
The much-cited feigned retreat exists only in dialogue; no trigger (retreat/lure/re-attack scripting) models it, so the player never has to execute the tactic the brief names as the core mechanic.
The 900-second 'nightfall' victory lets the player win by merely surviving, whereas historically dusk came only after the shield wall had broken and Harold was dead.
